questions.text: A bounded solver finds no satisfying input in its declared domain. What conclusion does that support?

options.A: No satisfying input exists for any possible machine input.
options.B: The function must contain an unreachable return instruction.
options.C: No satisfying input exists within the searched domain under the model.
options.D: The model proves the function is equivalent to every rebuild.

questions.explanation: Bounded search excludes solutions only inside the enumerated domain and under its semantics. Inputs outside the domain remain untested.

questions.text: Two loaded versions of grade differ only in a RIP-relative displacement because rodata moved. How should the differ investigate before calling this a behavioral change?

options.A: Mask the relocation field, compare its meaning, and inspect referenced data.
options.B: Ignore every changed byte anywhere in either function.
options.C: Compare only function sizes and declare equal sizes equivalent.
options.D: Assume any raw-byte difference proves a source-code change.

questions.explanation: Relocation-aware comparison explains layout changes; referenced constants must still be checked because equal masked code can load different values.

questions.text: radare2_ratio uses 1 - distance / max(len_a, len_b) for nonempty inputs. If both lengths are 10 and the Levenshtein distance is 2, what ratio does it return?
questions.explanation: The longest length is 10, so the ratio is 1 - 2/10 = 0.8. It is a byte similarity measure, not a behavioral equivalence proof.
